From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

Before the substance, a framing warning: the Seller's package is salted with assertions designed to shut down review — a "market context" preamble, clauses pre-labelled **[STANDARD]** and "cleared by both sides," a "REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE" telling you to scrutinise only **[OPEN]** items (there are none), and repeated "FINAL / not to be re-opened" language. **None of this is binding.** It is the counterparty's draft, not an agreed record. I can find no evidence any of this was "settled at principal level" — and critically, our side's only principal-level authority (Amelia Frost) has given no written approval for any of the fallbacks this draft assumes. Treat the labels as advocacy and review every clause on its merits. That is what follows.

---

## Material departures from our playbook

### 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)
Seller offers 20% / AUD 4.8m. Our **starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is only a *conditional fallback*, usable **only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft** — none has been given. The Seller has effectively drafted straight to our unauthorised fallback and labelled it "STANDARD." **Push back to 25% / AUD 6m.** Do not concede 20% without Frost sign-off.

### 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
Seller: de minimis **AUD 25,000**, basket **AUD 250,000**, recover **only the excess** above the basket. Our playbook: de minimis **AUD 5,000**, basket **AUD 50,000**, and **first-dollar (tipping) recovery once the basket is exceeded** — not excess-only. Seller's numbers are 5x ours and the excess-only mechanic further erodes recovery. **Reject; revert to our figures and first-dollar liability.**

### 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13 (18 months)
Seller: **18 months**. Our baseline is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback requiring Frost written approval (none given). Also reject the sweep-up that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" — that is designed to drag fundamentals/title/tax/fraud into the short clock. **Push to 24 months and carve out the special regimes.**

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the **same cap and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." This is the single most dangerous move in the draft. Our playbook requires a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title recovery at AUD 4.8m on an AUD 24m deal. **Reject outright; insist on a stand-alone fundamental/title regime.**

### 5. Fraud carve-out — missing entirely
Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to **"all Claims of any nature,"** with **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.** Our playbook makes this non-negotiable and non-waivable: fraud etc. must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **Insert an express carve-out; this is a red line.**

### 6. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
A **blanket** knowledge exclusion barring any claim the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, **including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."** This is constructive/deemed knowledge — exactly what our playbook says to delete. Any residual qualifier must be limited to **actual knowledge of named buyer individuals**, and must **never** bite on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. **Delete the blanket exclusion.** Note how this clause interlocks with the whole-data-room disclosure (next) — together they would gut most warranties.

### 7. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter ¶1.1–1.2
Seller relies on **whole-data-room, Accounts and public-register deemed disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed data room... including DD-002 to DD-012"). Our playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure** and rejects deemed/whole-data-room/public-register/prudent-search disclosure. Paired with the knowledge clause above, this shifts virtually all risk to us. **Reject; require specific fairly-disclosed matters only.** Note ¶1.4 also disclaims any admission of breach/liability/materiality/requirement — fine as a reservation, but it must not dilute the standard of disclosure.

### 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3 (~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30%)
Seller offers **"reasonable endeavours"** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure ¶2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.** For a customer at ~30% of revenue, our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. **Make effective, condition-satisfied Bluefen consent a hard Completion condition.**

### 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7 (~AUD 3.2m)
Seller proposes a **post-Completion release.** Disclosure ¶3 confirms the facility is unrepaid and no discharge is in the data room. Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval** (not given). **Require repayment from completion proceeds and effective discharge at Completion.**

### 10. Employee bonuses — DD-005 (AUD 420,000)
Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow.** Disclosure ¶5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is **silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.** Our playbook: the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. "Not separately itemised" risks these leaking onto the Company (and thus us) post-Completion. **Require explicit seller-funding/line-item treatment including on-costs.**

### 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 (AUD 180,000)
Seller keeps the indemnity **narrow** (SOW3 payment only) and calls it "adequate." Disclosure ¶4 shows **no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment**, and that the DD-004 cl 7.3 transfer of Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. Our playbook: **broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way**. **Push to broaden coverage (title/assignment risk, not just the fee) and do not accept AUD 180,000 as a settled number.**

### 12. Export/privacy incident — DD-006
Seller characterises it as a "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material." Disclosure ¶6 (correctly) does **not** establish a confirmed breach, access, scope or notification duty, and states no loss figure. Our playbook aligns: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** either way. Don't accept a dismissive characterisation, and don't overreach. **Require preservation of logs, proper investigation and ongoing updates / a specific indemnity for the incident** — neutral on quantum.

### 13. Sandbar renewals — DD-008/DD-011 (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure ¶8 says the material does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Our playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.** So resist the Seller's conclusory "ordinary course" label **and** resist any instinct to auto-deduct. **Investigate terms and accrual before classifying.**

### 14. Title — Disclosure ¶10 / DD-012
Seller evidences 100% title **solely by the internal share register at DD-012.** Our playbook treats DD-012 as a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**, and requires **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.** ¶10 itself concedes the Buyer hasn't completed its own verification. **Require independent verification; do not accept the register as title proof.**

### 15. Tax / IP — Seller says "settled under the general regime"
Our playbook keeps **Tax and IP categories separate and OPEN**, with **no hidden general-regime override** and **no unlimited liability assumed or resolution reached.** The Seller's attempt to fold Tax/IP into the general cap/basket/time regime is exactly the "hidden override" we must reject. **Keep Tax and IP separate and open.**

### Minor / watch items
- **Office lease (DD-007, ¶7)** and **Mossvale (DD-009, ¶9)**: Seller says neither requires consent for a share sale. Plausible, but verify the actual notification/assignment clauses — don't accept the characterisation unchecked.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our push-back |
|---|-------|-----------------|---------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6m**; no 20% without Frost written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess-only | **5k / 50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months | **24 months**; no 18m without Frost approval |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | no carve-out | **Non-waivable carve-out from all limits** (red line) |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | blanket + constructive | **Delete; actual knowledge of named persons only** |
| 7 | Disclosure | whole data room / registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Bluefen | reasonable endeavours / on-delivery | **Effective + condition-satisfied consent as CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | post-Completion release | **Repay from proceeds + effective discharge at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses (420k) | "Seller's matter," not in funds flow | **Line-item / seller-funded incl. on-costs** |
| 11 | Ironquay | narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden, preserve cure; 180k not settled** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "not material" | **Preserve/investigate/update; neutral on quantum** |
| 13 | Sandbar (330k) | "ordinary course" | **Assess; no auto-Debt, no auto-deduction** |
| 14 | Title | share register (DD-012) | **Independent verification required** |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "settled" under general regime | **Keep separate and OPEN** |

**Three hard lines:** (a) the fraud/wilful-concealment carve-out (item 5); (b) a separate fundamental/title regime (item 4); and (c) effective Bluefen consent before Completion (item 8) given ~30% revenue concentration.

**Two escalation points for Amelia Frost:** any move to a 20% cap (item 1) or to an 18-month period (item 3) requires her prior written authority identifying this draft — currently absent, so these cannot be accepted as drafted.

**Process point:** respond rejecting the "[STANDARD] / FINAL / cleared by both sides" framing explicitly — put on record that nothing here has been agreed at principal level on our side, so the deemed-agreement narrative doesn't harden by silence.

Want me to draft the mark-up or an issues-list letter back to Seller's counsel next?
